Michael Burry made his name betting against U.S. housing before 2008, but lately, he's been betting on something far less popular: Chinese stocks.

In his Substack newsletter, Cassandra Unchained, Burry said he has closed out his remaining bearish bets on the Nasdaq-100 and now holds roughly a quarter of his portfolio in cash. What's left is tilted abroad. Among his largest positions are MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI), Australian online retailer Temple & Webster and JD.com (NASDAQ:JD). Separately, stakes in Hong Kong-listed Tencent (OTC:TCEHY), BYD (OTC:BYDDY) and Meituan make up a little over a fifth of the portfolio.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Burry explained the overseas tilt simply by saying that U.S. stocks, in his view, are still expensive.

Michael Burry. Image source: Getty Images.

Why Burry Likes JD.com

JD.com is one of China's largest online retailers, known for owning its own warehouses and delivery network. Burry puts its intrinsic value at roughly $45 a share, and with the stock at $27.35 on Friday, that implies upside of more than 60%. JD also trades at about 0.17 times sales, its lowest level on record. Burry's exposure includes call options that expire in 2029.

His timing has looked good so far. Chinese stocks posted their biggest gain in two years on Friday after Beijing signaled more support for its markets, and JD rose about 4%. The shares remain well below their 52-week high of $34.30.

The Nvidia Twist

Burry isn't done with semiconductor stocks, either. He sold most of his bearish put options on Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) as the stock fell this month, while saying his original thesis "still has legs." His plan, he wrote, is to bet against Nvidia again "nearer $200/share during a period of market optimism. That time is not now." Nvidia closed Friday at $150.49.

Should You Follow Him?

Chinese stocks also carry risks U.S. stocks don't, including shifting government policy, U.S.-China trade fights, and accounting rules that give investors less visibility. JD's low valuation partly reflects those risks, along with fierce price competition in Chinese e-commerce.

Meanwhile, Burry can change course in days, and he often does, but the core idea is worth borrowing. When a profitable market leader trades at a record-low valuation because of fear rather than collapsing fundamentals, patient investors can be paid for waiting. If you want exposure to e-commerce stocks in China, JD is a reasonable place to start, as a small position you're prepared to hold for years. Investors who'd rather avoid China-specific risk can apply the same lesson at home: build a watch list of quality tech stocks that have been knocked down, and buy in stages.

The S&P 500 fell 3.7% on Friday, November 20, its seventh straight losing session and its longest losing streak since the pandemic crash, according to Jared Blikre, global markets and data editor at Yahoo Finance. The index closed in correction territory, about $8 trillion below its October 6 record, and the Nasdaq-100 dropped 5.6% to sit close to the 20% decline that defines a bear market. By the same editor's estimate, consumer prices rose about 4% in the year through October, up from about 2.8% a year earlier.

Inflation Keeps the Fed on Course

That backdrop explains why traders are not betting on relief. Blikre wrote that the bond market prices a 92% chance that the Federal Reserve raises interest rates at its December 9 meeting. Fed Governor Lisa Cook said, "Waiting longer to implement rate increases risks getting behind the curve."

The inflation data has not helped. The core PCE report on November 25 showed prices up 3.3% from a year earlier, hotter than expected, which left a December hike all but certain with more possible early next year. History is a mixed guide for what follows. Blikre noted that all eight S&P 500 corrections since 1950 that began with inflation rising a point or more went on to become bear markets, while 12 of 16 corrections since 1989 were erased within a year. Investors who hold through drawdowns can find more ideas in our ranking of blue chip stocks to buy and hold for three years.

What Strategists Watch for a Bottom

Goldman Sachs strategist Ben Snider named three conditions that would support a market bottom and recovery in remarks Yahoo Finance reported on November 23: news that raises confidence in future earnings from AI investment, a dovish signal from the Fed, or a major decline in investor positioning. He stopped short of an all-clear, recommending that investors diversify with select defensive stocks and companies with strong buybacks.

Other strategists are weighing the damage differently. Evercore ISI strategist Julian Emanuel wrote that the firm is "not cavalier about the damage done in markets and the risks ahead," while arguing that the bull market is not over. The volatility index, a gauge of expected market swings, closed at 35.89 on November 20, up 26.2% in a single session.

The next test arrives quickly. The Fed meets on December 9, and Blikre wrote that traders have trimmed the number of rate hikes they expect through September 2027 to about 2.4 from three. He said the tilt toward foreign stocks is due to high U.S. valuations. His JD exposure includes call options that expire as late as 2029, which shows he is prepared to wait a long time. On Wednesday, the NASDAQ Composite went down as much as 4.64% intraday before it closed down 0.62%, which shows how volatile the market Burry is investing in has become.

Burry disclosed which stocks he picked and what he paid for them. Several now trade near or below the entry levels he gave.

Expensive Puts Pushed Burry Toward Stocks

He calls the long tilt temporary "because I am continuing to assess short opportunities." The only bearish options he still holds are puts on a software stock and a life insurer. He has also sold the final half of his NASDAQ index puts.

He said puts have become "very expensive" as the VIX rises. That leaves shorting common stock as his main bearish tool, a trade he called "asymmetric the wrong way."

Michael Burry said about 25% of his portfolio is in cash. Most of it came from winning puts plus new money, and he is working to invest it.

Morgan Stanley Cut Its MercadoLibre Target. It Still Sees 66% Upside ©@Nataliya Vaitkevich from Pexels via Canva
Key Takeaways

Morgan Stanley cut its MercadoLibre price target to $2,350 from $2,450 on Nov. 23 and kept its Overweight rating, leaving the target 66% above the stock.

MercadoLibre's third-quarter revenue rose 45%, but operating income fell 6% as it spent more on free shipping, warehouse space and marketing in Brazil.

On 2028 earnings estimates, $2,350 is 32x, far below the stock's five-year average of 61x, so the target doesn't need a higher multiple.

Analysts have cut those 2028 estimates since the third-quarter report, and Sea's Shopee keeps pushing in Brazil. Until margins recover, $2,350 looks like a best case.

MercadoLibre (MELI:NASDAQ) has lost 40% since its late-January high, and Morgan Stanley just cut its price target for the third time since March. Analyst Andrew Ruben kept his Overweight rating on Nov. 23, and his new $2,350 target sits 66% above the stock.

Record growth, thinner margins

On Nov. 4, MercadoLibre's third-quarter revenue rose 45% to $10.75 billion. But operating income fell 6% to $676 million, a 6.3% margin, and GAAP EPS of $8.83 missed the $9.27 analysts expected. The company blamed more free shipping, warehouse space added ahead of the holiday peak and heavier affiliate marketing in Brazil.

And MercadoLibre has competition in Brazil. Sea Limited (SE:NYSE) said Brazil was again Shopee's fastest-growing market in the third quarter. Shopee's adjusted EBITDA rose 45% to $269.2 million across all its markets, so Sea has the profit to keep pushing.

Morgan Stanley is still a believer

In May, Ruben wrote that the firm had "again underestimated MELI's investment scope" and that 2026 was "shaping up as a lost year for EBIT."

Other bulls are trimming too: Bank of America cut its target to $2,000 from $2,400 on Nov. 19 and kept its Buy. TIKR tracks 25 analysts on MercadoLibre, and their average target has fallen to $2,153 from $2,850 a year ago:

Michael Burry has sold his remaining Nasdaq-100 put options and shifted toward undervalued stocks.

Burry's largest holdings include MercadoLibre, Temple & Webster and JD.com.

Burry's Nvidia call options have doubled, but he could short the stock again only near $200.

The "Big Short" investor Michael Burry has closed his remaining Nasdaq-100 put options, signaling a shift toward bullish bets even as market volatility rises. The investor is holding roughly 25% cash, favoring undervalued stocks while considering a fresh short position in Nvidia (NVDA) near $200.

Michael Burry's Bearish Bets Shrink As Cash Position Grows

In his latest Substack post, Michael Burry said his investment now leans more toward undervalued stocks as he scales back bearish bets and builds a sizable cash reserve.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

"Today, as tech stocks were weak, I sold the rest (final half) of the Nasdaq 100 (NDX) put position," said Burry.

His only outstanding bearish options positions are tied to Palantir Technologies (PLTR) and MetLife (MET). Burry added that he is still evaluating potential short opportunities but currently prefers owning stocks. Around 25% of his portfolio is held in cash.

Overseas Stocks Lead Burry's Biggest Positions

MercadoLibre (MELI), Temple & Webster Group and JD.com Inc. (JD) currently rank among his largest holdings. His JD.com exposure also includes call options with expiration dates extending to 2029.

"This international focus at the top is not uncommon in my portfolio strategy, and is a byproduct of continued high valuations in the United States."

Burry's other investments include Adobe (ADBE), Birkenstock (BIRK), Deckers Outdoor (DECK), Lululemon Athletica (LULU), and PayPal Holdings Inc. (PYPL). His smaller investments include Hong Kong-listed businesses such as BYD, Tencent, and Meituan. Together, these positions now represent slightly more than one-fifth of his portfolio.

Nvidia Short Could Return Near $200

Burry said he continues to hold call options on Nvidia, which have already doubled in value. "My plan is to short Nvidia again nearer $200/share during a period of market optimism. That time is not now."

"So for now, I am long undervalued common stocks, LEAP calls and preferred stock, with a modest cash pile."

On Monday, after Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia's CEO, Burry suggested that if Huang helps revive the stock market, regulators might lose interest in investigating the company.
